title: Romulus and Remus
objective: After this level you can retell Rome’s founding legend and explain why Romans valued it.
summary: Legend says twin sons of Mars, nursed by a she-wolf, founded Rome, and Romulus killed Remus. Historians treat it as legend, not history.

cards.headline: Rome’s origin story: twins, a wolf and a murder.
cards.body: Not exactly a bedtime story. Yet the wolf became a symbol of Rome itself.

cards.headline: Raised by a wolf
cards.body: In the legend, the twins Romulus and Remus were sons of the god Mars. They were abandoned as babies, and a she-wolf found them and nursed them. Rome turned that moment into its emblem: the she-wolf feeding the twins became one of the city’s best-known symbols. Most cities don’t put a wild predator in the family photo. Rome made it the cover shot.

cards.headline: A city named in blood
cards.body: The twins grew up, and their new city came between them. They quarreled over it, and Romulus killed Remus. The winner got the naming rights: the city was named Rome, after Romulus. Imagine your hometown being named after whichever sibling won the argument. Romans didn’t have to imagine it.

cards.headline: Legend, not history
cards.body: Romans had a second origin story, too. They traced their ancestry to Aeneas, a Trojan prince who, in legend, fled the fall of Troy to Italy. Historians treat both stories as legend, because they were written down centuries after the events they describe. So why learn them? Because they show how Romans saw themselves. A legend won’t tell you what happened, but it tells you who a people wanted to be.

mascot.line: If you keep one thing here: a legend shows who Romans wanted to be, not what happened.

cards.headline: Founding legend: known
learned: Legend: twin sons of Mars founded Rome
Romulus killed Remus; the city took his name

questions.prompt: In the legend, what nursed the abandoned Romulus and Remus?
questions.explanation: A she-wolf found and nursed the twins, an image that became a symbol of Rome.

questions.prompt: Why do historians treat the Romulus and Remus story as legend?

options.label: It was written down centuries after the events
Archaeology shows Rome was never founded
options.rationale: Rome was founded; the story is the question.

questions.explanation: The founding stories were recorded long after the events, so they tell us more about how Romans saw themselves.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: Romans dated the founding to 753 BCE. How did the legend explain the city’s name?

options.label: It was named after the Tiber
It was named after the she-wolf

questions.explanation: After Romulus killed Remus, the new city took Romulus’s name.
